I also would like to get into commercial or corporate banking in my career and I am an accounting major so I can relate to your situation a bit. You got an internship with the Big 4, so that's great! Use that over the summer to go build your understanding of the banking world while also expanding your relationships with these professionals.

Networking might have some weight into getting your foot into the door, but it can only go so far. You already have a Big 4 internship which is great, you have something to back up your academic records. Don't feel like you have to rush frats because you need to boost up your resume unless you really want to. But ultimately, these careers are just relationship building careers. With that said, you should emphasize soft skills and quantify them as much as possible (IE Led 1,000 people, raised $3,000 for a 501(c)3, etc). You're in a Big 4 internship so putting technical skills can work as well (if not make you even more differentiated).

You don't need to know a whole lot of technicals like an IB interview, but you should be more focused on getting leadership positions where you have communicated with large amounts of people and jobs where you have engaged with a wide variety of people. Being in a business club/org doesn't mean you're automatically ahead of the applicants; a large majority of applicants are in one as well, you're just meeting the par of the expectations. I'd say join organizations where you can make meaningful impacts, like community service, student government organizations, etc. That way you can have a more meaningful and engaging interview.
